blocking.title: Fork rule is bypassed by checkout: the evidence worktree runs git hooks the PR commits, because core.hooksPath=.husky/_ resolves inside the checked-out tree
blocking.failurePath: Input: pr-gate is run on a PR whose head.repo.full_name is not xiechimon/pacman, and whose head tracks an executable `.husky/_/post-checkout` (or `.husky/_/reference-transaction`), added with `git add -f`. State: this clone's shared .git/config sets `core.hooksPath=.husky/_`, written by the root `prepare: husky` script. The setting is relative, so in any worktree git resolves it to `<worktree>/.husky/_`. Code: line 182 tells the evidence reviewer to run `git checkout --detach ${headSha}` 'after the fetch'. It only forbids installing and running for a fork head, and checkout is not forbidden. Line 267 gives the evidence skeptics the same checkout permission. Result: the checkout writes `.husky/_/post-checkout` from the fork into the worktree, and git then runs it as the post-checkout hook. Any later ref update in that worktree also runs the PR's reference-transaction hook, including the reviewer's own `git update-ref -d` cleanup. Fork-controlled code therefore runs with the session's gh and git credentials. That is exactly what the fork rule (lines 182 and 267, spec 28 §7.5 line 256, PR Risk section) says cannot happen, and it happens even when the agent obeys the prompt. Fix: for a fork head, do no checkout at all and read with `git show`/`git diff` only. Otherwise prefix every git command in the evidence worktree with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`.
blocking.evidence: `git config --show-origin --get-all core.hooksPath` -> `file:/home/user/pacman/.git/config .husky/_`. Scratch repro on git 2.43.0: clone with `core.hooksPath .husky/_`, `git worktree add --detach wt main` (wt has no .husky), then `git checkout --detach <commit tracking .husky/_/post-checkout 100755>` -> the hook wrote `HOOK-RAN:.husky/_/post-checkout`. None of runs 1-9 in docs/verify/1401 raises hooksPath or post-checkout.
skeptics: I confirmed the mechanism at 9460e045, with one caveat about this container. In .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js, line 182 tells the evidence reviewer to run `git checkout --detach ${headSha}` right after the fetch. The fork rule that follows forbids only installing and running, not checking out. Line 267 gives the evidence skeptics the same checkout permission. Nothing in the file mentions hooksPath or disables hooks. The worktree isolation uses git worktrees of this clone (.claude/worktrees/wf_*), and those share .git/config; extensions.worktreeConfig is not set. The root package.json has `prepare: husky`, and husky 9.1.7 (node_modules/husky/index.js) runs `git config core.hooksPath .husky/_`, which is a relative path. pnpm runs this root script on install, and .npmrc does not exist, so nothing sets ignore-scripts. That means the gate's own `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` step for a same-repo PR rewrites the shared config to the relative value. I reproduced the attack in a scratch repo on git 2.43.0. I set core.hooksPath to `.husky/_`, created a worktree with --detach from main (it has no .husky), and checked out a commit that tracks executable `.husky/_/post-checkout` and `.husky/_/reference-transaction`, added with `git add -f`. Both hooks ran, with cwd set to the worktree. A later `git update-ref -d` ran reference-transaction again. That is code chosen by the fork running with the session's credentials, even though the agent obeyed the prompt. The PROTECTED glob `**/.husky/**` only routes the merge decision to the user, and the hook has already run during review by then. Caveat: the reviewer said this clone's config holds `.husky/_`, but right now /home/user/pacman/.git/config holds the absolute `/home/user/pacman/.husky/_` (file rewritten 08:15:21). With an absolute path the fork's hooks did not run in my contrast repro, so the attack is closed in this container at this moment. It is still the steady state after any husky install, including the gate's own install step. Spec 28 §7.5 also says to run pr-gate only on this session's own PRs, which lowers the chance of exposure. It does not make the script's fork rule true. Fix: skip checkout for a fork head and read with `git show`, or run git with `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` in the evidence worktree.

I confirmed the failure at 9460e045. The fetched head ref resolved to that SHA.

1. The prompt allows checkout of a fork head. Line 182 of .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js tells the evidence reviewer to run `git checkout --detach ${headSha}` after the fetch. For a fork, it only says "install nothing and run nothing from the PR", which does not forbid checkout. Line 267 explicitly lets the evidence skeptics `git checkout --detach`, and its fork clause has the same gap. Nothing earlier in the script stops fork PRs. Lines 120-145 only validate the arguments. The protected-path routing (`**/.husky/**`) is decided after the reviewers have already run, so it does not help.

2. The worktree shares the main clone's config. The isolation worktrees are git worktrees of the shared clone: `git worktree list` shows the `.claude/worktrees/wf_*` worktrees with detached HEADs. `extensions.worktreeConfig` is not set, so every worktree reads core.hooksPath from the shared .git/config.

3. The hooks path is relative by default. Root package.json at the head has `"prepare": "husky"`. husky 9's index.js runs `git config core.hooksPath ${d}/_` with `d = '.husky'`, which writes the relative value `.husky/_`. The same prompt sends same-repo PRs through `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which runs root `prepare` and writes that relative value back into the shared config. Git resolves a relative hooksPath against the root of the worktree the hook runs in, so it points at the PR's own `.husky/_`. The head tree tracks only .husky/banned.txt and .husky/pre-commit. The main clone's `.husky/_/.gitignore` contains `*`, so an attacker would have to add files there with `git add -f`, which is easy.

4. I reproduced it with scratch repos on the same git 2.43.0 (repro since deleted):
   - Setup: a main repo with `core.hooksPath .husky/_`, and a commit that tracks `.husky/_/post-checkout` and `.husky/_/reference-transaction` with mode 100755.
   - `git worktree add --detach wt main` ran no hooks.
   - In wt, `git checkout --detach <that commit>` ran the commit's reference-transaction hook (prepared, then committed) and then its post-checkout hook. Both ran with cwd set to the worktree.
   - A later `git update-ref` and the `git update-ref -d` cleanup ran the PR's reference-transaction hook again.

   So code controlled by the fork runs with the session's credentials, even when the agent follows the prompt exactly. That contradicts the fork rule on lines 182 and 267.

One caveat: when I checked, this clone's .git/config had an absolute value, `core.hooksPath=/home/user/pacman/.husky/_`. The file's mtime was 08:19:02 today, seconds before I looked, so something rewrote it recently. With an absolute value, the wrapper `.husky/_/h` looks for `/home/user/pacman/.husky/post-checkout`, which does not exist, so this specific vector would be inert right now. That state is not stable: husky's default, and any `pnpm install` the same prompt triggers for same-repo PRs, writes the relative value back. So the gap in the prompt itself is real.

suggestions.title: Evidence skeptics get no port assignment; two run in parallel against a playwright config with reuseExistingServer: true
suggestions.failurePath: The evidence reviewer prompt (line 182) assigns VERIFY_PORT=8793, VERIFY_WEB_PORT=5275 and E2E_AFFECTED_PORT=8397. The skeptic prompt (line 267) contains only readRules, the finding and the worktree and fork note. When the evidence dimension reports a blocking finding, two skeptics start at once through parallel (lines 263-277), each in its own worktree. If both re-run e2e:affected, both take the default 8398 (scripts/e2e-affected.mjs:36). apps/web/playwright.config.ts:28 has reuseExistingServer: true, so the second skeptic quietly tests the first skeptic's preview server. If that server stops mid-run, the second run fails. If the main session or another lane holds 8398 (CLAUDE.md names it as the e2e:affected default), both skeptics test another branch's build. A disrupted skeptic is told to set refuted=true when it cannot confirm, so the vote depends on timing, not on the head.
suggestions.evidence: pr-gate.js line 182 sets the ports for review:evidence only. The skeptic template at line 267 adds only the checkout and fork sentences for evidence. scripts/e2e-affected.mjs:36 reads `process.env.E2E_PORT ?? process.env.E2E_AFFECTED_PORT ?? '8398'`. apps/web/playwright.config.ts:26-28 runs vite preview --strictPort with reuseExistingServer: true. Fix: pass distinct ports per skeptic index (for example 8394+i) in the evidence skeptic prompt.

suggestions.title: Paths only in the safety reviewer's deletedFiles are never matched against PROTECTED or the auto-merge set
suggestions.failurePath: seenFiles and unlistedFiles come from safety.changedFiles only (lines 326-327). safety.deletedFiles feeds only the deleted-test regex (lines 338-341), and safety.binaryFiles feeds only the binary rule. Suppose a caller list misses a deletion and the safety reviewer puts that path in deletedFiles but not in changedFiles. For example, the caller passes changedFiles ['apps/server/src/x.ts'] and safety returns changedFiles ['apps/server/src/x.ts'] and deletedFiles ['.husky/pre-commit']. The gate then returns go true, mergedBy 'auto-merge' and empty humanReasons. This needs two slips at once, but the script already treats the reviewer's lists as the cross-check on the caller.
suggestions.evidence: Stub probe against the head copy (the self-check harness with that safety review): `safety-deleted-only => go true mergedBy auto-merge []`. Fix: build seenFiles from safety.changedFiles plus safety.deletedFiles and safety.binaryFiles, so these paths reach unlistedFiles and the D4 match.

suggestions.title: Directory-class globs miss an entry named exactly like the directory (a symlinked .claude, scripts or drizzle inside the auto-merge set)
suggestions.failurePath: `**/.claude/**` compiles to ^(?:.*/)?\.claude/.*$ and needs a character after `.claude/`. A PR that adds the symlink `apps/web/src/.claude` pointing to `payload`, plus `apps/web/src/payload/skills/x/SKILL.md`, changes two paths that both sit in apps/*/src/** and match no PROTECTED glob. On checkout, apps/web/src/.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md then exists, a file ADR 0021 D4 class 1 protects at any depth. The same holds for `**/scripts/**`, `**/.husky/**`, `**/.pi/**`, `**/.cursor/**` and `**/drizzle/**`. Real impact depends on whether a tool reads that nested directory, so this is not blocking.
suggestions.evidence: Stub probe against the head copy. Each of apps/web/src/.claude, apps/server/src/scripts, apps/server/src/.husky and apps/server/src/drizzle as the only changed file returned go true and mergedBy auto-merge. Fix: also match the bare directory name (for example a `(/.*)?$` tail for directory classes), or route symlink and gitlink entries (mode 120000 or 160000) to the user.

suggestions.title: Three commit subjects have no ticket, and the AGENTS.md squash recipe that ADR 0021 D2 points to returns one of them for this PR
suggestions.failurePath: ca088ce, 3944905 and 662cbd9 have subjects of the form `docs: spec 28 ...` with no `(1401)`, which breaks AGENTS.md:61. ADR 0021 D2 (line 35) tells a person merging in the GitHub UI or CLI to follow the AGENTS.md squash recipe. That recipe (AGENTS.md:70) takes `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/pulls/<n>/commits -q '.[0].commit.message'`, which returns ca088ce for #1410. A merger who follows it lands the subject `docs: spec 28 自举闭环计划…` on main, with no `closes #1401`, so #1401 stays open. Two things guard against this: the PR body's Issues section supplies a ready squash message, and the repo default (PR_TITLE + COMMIT_MESSAGES) would carry e5414a2's `closes #1401`. History cannot be rewritten because force-push is banned. The merger must use the body's message, not `.[0]`. D2 could also say that the recipe only works when the first commit carries the ticket and the closing line. Run 9 raised this too, and it is still open.
suggestions.evidence: git log subjects: ca088ce 'docs: spec 28 自举闭环计划（…）', 3944905 'docs: spec 28 补云端会话变体（…）', 662cbd9 'docs: spec 28 加 workflow 编排（…）'. `gh api repos/xiechimon/pacman/pulls/1410/commits --jq '.[0].sha'` = ca088ce. `closes #1401` appears only in e5414a2. Repo settings: squash_merge_commit_title=PR_TITLE, squash_merge_commit_message=COMMIT_MESSAGES.

suggestions.title: docs/pr-review.md now allows a detached checkout that AGENTS.md:96 still calls forbidden by a hard rule, with no pointer from AGENTS.md
suggestions.failurePath: AGENTS.md:96 (CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it) says 「不切分支看 diff」是硬要求. The new section at docs/pr-review.md:14-16 lets pr-gate's evidence reviewer and its skeptics run `git checkout --detach <headSha>` in their own worktree. AGENTS.md:113 (User Override) asks for an explicit user confirmation of the form 「我同意打破 No X 规则，因为 Y」 before any rule is broken. The authorization this PR cites is the goal prompt's 「按 §7.5 用 workflow 编排子代理」 (spec 28:208, 232). The §7.5 text it refers to has said 「在独立 worktree 里 detach 到 headSha」 since 662cbd9. An agent that reads only AGENTS.md (pr-gate's own rules reviewer is told to check against CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md) will see the evidence dimension as a rule break. The isolation does protect what the rule is for, the shared worktree, so no wrong result follows. Suggest a one-line pointer from AGENTS.md:96 to the pr-review.md exception, or recording the user's override in that form.

suggestions.title: ADR 0021 premortem names 'agent changes tests to pass its own gate' but D4 covers only deleting tests, not weakening them in place
suggestions.failurePath: The premortem row 'agent 改测试或改闸，让自己过闸' is guarded by 'D4 保护路径与「删测试即 human」'. A PR that edits apps/server/test/x.test.ts to drop an assertion is not a deletion and stays inside the auto-merge set (apps/*/test/**). D4 routes it to auto-merge; only a reviewer's judgment (pr-gate's tests dimension, and later P3's automated review) stands between it and a merge. The row overstates what D4 enforces in code for P3/P4 to build on.

suggestions.title: PR body commands reach the evidence reviewer's shell; the 'only PRs this session wrote' limit is not in the code
suggestions.failurePath: For a same-repo head, the evidence reviewer runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, which runs the root `prepare: husky` and the allowBuilds postinstalls. It then re-runs up to three commands quoted in the PR body's Verified section, for example a 'gate script' such as `node scripts/<file the PR adds>.mjs`. Both happen with the session's credentials. Spec 28 §7.5 line 256 limits pr-gate to PRs this session wrote, but the script does not check the PR author or the head ref. A same-repo PR from another collaborator, or a body shaped by an issue the session took in under D5, therefore gets PR text and PR code into a shell. The Risk section names this as a prompt rule. A code check (head.ref prefix `claude/` and user.login) would make the limit hold.

suggestions.title: D4 auto-merge set covers the #1256 merge blocks and agent tool switches
suggestions.failurePath: Take a small PR that removes the `MERGE_HUMAN_ONLY_COPY` return in apps/server/src/services/chief-tools.ts:870 or the 403 in apps/server/src/services/mcp-face.ts:365, or that edits AGENT_TOOL_SWITCHES in apps/server/src/routes-agents.ts. It matches `apps/*/src/**` and no PROTECTED class, so it gets mergedBy 'auto-merge'. Under D7 the bootstrap session would then enable auto-merge on a go. ADR 0021 D1's guarantee that `human` keeps the #1256 blocks would then rest only on reviewers noticing. The PR's Risk section names this and defers it to P3/P4. Listing these files, or packages/shared/src/records/message.ts, as protected would make D1 mechanical.

checked.correctness:
Head confirmed: refs/pr-gate/1410/correctness/head resolved to 9460e045890583341c0088f1575313d99d5781ca (merge base 23a39da). I read these files in full at the head: .claude/workflows/pr-gate.js (384 lines), scripts/pr-gate-selfcheck.mjs (841 lines), the .github/workflows/ci.yml check job around the new step, and the .gitignore, docs/pr-review.md, ADR 0018, ADR 0021 and spec 28 diffs. The script handles all of these and fails closed.
